correction.text: the Wuxi-Suzhou core of the early Wu, -750..-585

keyframe_review.note: 193,280 km2 for -750..-551, bounding 116.1-122.0E, 29.5-34.9N (Jiangsu, Anhui, Zhejiang): far too large for the years before the rise, since 'Wu rose to power in the 6th century BC' and its 'first documented interaction with the Spring and Autumn states was in 584'. Correction: the Wuxi-Suzhou core for -750..-585; the Cliopatria shape is kept for -584..-551 (new keyframe wu_-584). The infobox has no area; the ratio cannot be taken.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 750 shape kept from 584, the rise of Wu

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for -584..-551: Wu 'gradually grew stronger, and in 584 BC defeated Chu for the first time and annexed the Chu city of Zhoulai'; Cliopatria's 193 k km2 shape is kept for these years as unverified (no page opened gives Wu's frontier in the 6th century).

193,280 km2 for -550..-483 (from 482 see wu_-480): after the rise, the conquests of Xu (512) and Qi (484), and the brief occupation of Ying (506-505). No Wu frontier is given on the pages opened; the shape is kept as unverified. It overlaps Cliopatria's Yue shape of 500-481 (539 cells), which the Wu page does not support: Yue annexed Wu only in 473.

correction.text: unchanged but valid only for -482..-474; the state ends in 473

keyframe_review.note: 82,848 km2 for -480..-451: the 416 cells north of the 539 that Cliopatria hands to Yue in 480. The page says Yue 'launched a surprise attack on Wu in 482 BC and conquered the capital' and 'Yue absorbed the state in 473', so this remnant holds for -482..-474 only; from 473 Wu no longer exists (the ledger), and Cliopatria's years -473..-451 are wrong.

ledger.note: 12th century BC: Taibo founds Wu in the Yangtze delta (infobox 'Foundation by Taibo: 12th century BC'). The page gives only the century; -1100 is a placeholder for it, and the land is the infobox capital 'modern-day Wuxi and Suzhou, Jiangsu province'. Fixed in fx-46 (requests R015, R017): the bare name 'Suzhou' resolves to Suzhou in Anhui, so the second disc is now fixed on Suzhou, Jiangsu (120.62 E, 31.30 N); the page: first capital Meili 'in modern Wuxi', 'later moved to Gusu (probably in modern Suzhou)'.

584: Wu rebels against Chu and annexes the Chu city of Zhoulai. 'in 584 BC defeated Chu for the first time and annexed the Chu city of Zhoulai'; the Wu page: 'In 584 BC, Wu rebelled against Chu upon the advice of Wuchen, a Jin minister'. The page does not locate Zhoulai (the researcher's reading is the Huai near modern Huainan).

512: Wu conquers Xu. Xu page: 'Reduced to its heartland, Xu was eventually conquered by Wu in 512 BC'; infobox 'Conquered by Wu: 512 BC'; the Spring and Autumn table 'Xu 512 BCE: to Wu'. The Chu dossier also claims Xu for 512, from the Chu page.

506: King Helü invades Chu and Wu takes the Chu capital Ying. 'In 506 BC, during the reign of King Zhao of Chu, King Helü decided to invade Chu'; Wu reached Ying after five victories 'and captured it' (no year for the capture); King Zhao fled to Yun and Sui.

505: Qin and Chu drive Wu out of Ying. 'In 505 BC, the Qin and Chu armies jointly defeated Wu in several battles'; 'King Zhao of Chu then returned to the capital Ying'; 'Wu was unable to hold on to its territorial gains'. Helü also had to go home to put down Fugai.

region.text: the capital and the southern core of Wu, taken by Yue

ledger.note: 482: while Fuchai holds a conference, Yue takes Wu's capital. Wu page: Yue 'launched a surprise attack on Wu in 482 BC and conquered the capital'; Spring and Autumn page: 'In 482, King Fuchai of Wu held an interstate conference to solidify his power base, but Yue captured the Wu capital.' Wu's core is the 539 cells that Cliopatria gives Yue in 480. (Reviewer ea-01-c: confidence lowered from 3 to 2; the Wu and Spring and Autumn pages name only 'the capital'/'the city', not the 539-cell region.)

region.text: the capital and the southern core of Wu

ledger.note: 473: the siege of the capital ends and Yue annexes Wu. 'Fuchai rushed back but was besieged and died when the city fell in 473.' (Reviewer ea-01-c: confidence lowered from 3 to 2; the Wu and Spring and Autumn pages name only 'the capital'/'the city', not the 539-cell region.)

473: Yue absorbs Wu and King Goujian becomes hegemon. 'Over the next decade, Wu was unable to recover and Yue absorbed the state in 473 BC'; infobox 'Defeated by Yue: 473 BC'; the Spring and Autumn page: 'King Goujian destroyed and annexed Wu in 473'.

wars.name: Wu conquest of Xu
wars.outcome: King Helü conquered Xu and extinguished the state.

wars.name: Battle of Boju and the Wu occupation of Ying
wars.outcome: Wu, with Cai and Tang, took Ying in 506; Qin and Chu defeated Wu in 505 and King Zhao returned to Ying.

wars.name: Wu-Qi war (Ailing)
wars.outcome: Wu 'turned to other campaigns, defeating the State of Qi in 484 BC'; no border changed.

wars.name: Yue's conquest of Wu
wars.outcome: Yue captured the capital in 482 while Fuchai was at a conference; Wu could not recover and was absorbed in 473.

certainty.note: Wu's frontiers are city territories and marcher lands; the 6th-century conquests (Xu, Zhoulai, Ying) have no boundaries on the pages opened.

notes: One dossier for Cliopatria's 'Wu' (-750..-451). Wikidata Q274488 is shared with Eastern Wu (the Three Kingdoms state, 222-280 CE), a different state: not merged. Cliopatria's rows are wrong in three ways: (1) the 193 k km2 shape stands for 750-551 though Wu 'rose to power in the 6th century'; (2) the Yue row of 500-481 overlaps Wu's core by 539 cells although Yue annexed Wu only in 473 (for the Yue group: Yue's first shape should start 482/473); (3) Wu's remnant shape runs to 451, 22 years past 473. Not settled: the extent of Wu in the 6th-5th centuries (no frontier on any page opened); the location of Zhoulai; the dates of the capital moves; the starting year (the century only). Page budget (1-2) was exceeded by two pages (Boju, Xu) because the 506 and 512 events needed them. Gazetteer: no unknown names used (Wuxi, Suzhou, Huainan, Jingzhou resolve).
